newsitem.title: HUNGARY: MAIZE, WHEAT FUTURES SLIDE ON BUDAPEST GRAIN MKT.
newsitem.headline: MAIZE, WHEAT FUTURES SLIDE ON BUDAPEST GRAIN MKT.

text.p: Maize and wheat futures continued yesterday's falling trend on the grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) in what dealers saw as profit-taking after last week's surge in prices.

"There was a slight bearish mood for both maize and milling wheat," said Gabor Herczeg of La Salle. "It wasn't so much oversupply as a case of profit-taking after last week's rallies," he said, adding he believed the market was still overvalued.
Maize for May delivery ended at 18,500, down 150 while July fell 100 to 18,500. March delivery was stable at 19,190.
Milling wheat prices showed a similar pattern, falling for all maturities except March, which rose by 10.
Turnover was a modest 244 million forints, or 590 lots.
Herczeg said further falls could be slowed by the strengthening dollar which is making Hungarian prices more attractive.
"As the dollar surges the Budapest market becomes more interesting for foreign buyers," he said.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
